# Mother Tongues Blog

> A community resource for indigenous language revitalization through open-source language technology tools and tutorials.

Mother Tongues Blog provides practical guides and documentation for language technologists, educators, and community members working on indigenous language preservation and digital tools. The blog covers grapheme-to-phoneme conversion, typesetting, voice recording, and interactive language games.

## Key Topics

- language revitalization
- indigenous languages
- grapheme-to-phoneme (g2p)
- open-source tools
- language technology
- Wordle games
- syllabics typesetting
- LaTeX
- voice recording
- Mozilla Common Voice
- Cree syllabics
- text normalization
- language documentation
- GitHub

## Grapheme-to-Phoneme (G2P) Tutorials

- [G2P Part 6: Pre-processing Mapping for Text Normalization](https://blog.mothertongues.org/g2p-preprocess): G2P tutorial: Text normalization with g2p pre-processing mapping
- [G2P Part 7: Contributing a New Mapping](https://blog.mothertongues.org/g2p-contributing): G2P tutorial: Contributing grapheme-to-phoneme mappings to g2p
- [Preventing Feeding of G2P Rules with Case](https://blog.mothertongues.org/g2p-case-feeding): Tutorial: Prevent feeding between g2p grapheme-to-phoneme rules

## Language Technology Tutorials

- [How to Make a Wordle Clone for Your Language](https://blog.mothertongues.org/wordle): Tutorial: Create a Wordle clone for your language with GitHub
- [Typesetting Syllabics (and More) in LaTeX](https://blog.mothertongues.org/typesetting-syllabics-and-more-in-latex): Tutorial by Rebecca Knowles: LaTeX typesetting for syllabics fonts
